submission_template.user_id_type: str, exact CSV value; no numeric conversion

timezone_evidence.absolute_timezone: unknown; CSV timestamps contain no offsets or zone name
timezone_evidence.evidence_scope: matching missing hour, all 117 view duration discrepancies and all 394 crossing adjacent-airing gaps; not proof of a named timezone or content-level clock synchronisation

limitations: Absolute timezone cannot be established from these CSVs; no timezone name or UTC conversion is asserted. The one-hour spring clock jump is normalised using training-data evidence in both sources.
Most airtime has tv_show_id=0; absence of a labelled interaction is not proof of no watching.
Different titles/metadata under one programme ID may represent episodes or data inconsistency; IDs are not merged by title.
A qualifying overlap is a proxy for watching, not evidence of enjoyment.
Final training on weeks11–30 should recompute airing thresholds over the combined window; simply adding two split aggregates may miss boundary fragments.
Resource measurements cover this full profiling/preparation process and are not comparable to a bare CSV read benchmark.

parameters.candidate_policy: positive-duration nonzero labelled airings intersecting the calendar period across all schedule files
parameters.clock_gap_normalisation: f(t)=naive_calendar_seconds(t)-3600 for t>=2020-03-29 04:00; identity earlier; timestamps in the missing hour are rejected
parameters.conflicting_schedule_policy: all conflicting simultaneous item IDs, including zero+labelled, are ambiguous; excluded from item seconds
parameters.cross_channel_same_item_policy: union watched seconds; merge strictly overlapping accepted airing spans for watch_count
parameters.implementation: Python standard library only; no DuckDB, pandas, numpy or ML dependencies
parameters.index: per-channel sweep-line canonicalisation; disjoint sorted arrays; bisect then output-sensitive scan
parameters.index_complexity: O(S log S) preprocessing; O(log S_channel + number_of_intersected_segments) per view
parameters.join: channel equality and half-open interval overlap
parameters.last_watch_time_semantics: exclusive end of the last accepted observed interval, not a programme end prediction
parameters.schedule_duplicates_policy: union strictly overlapping same-item airings on one channel; adjacent airings remain distinct
parameters.source_of_view_duration: stop_time - start_time after the empirically verified clock-gap normalisation; original duraton is retained for EDA
parameters.split_policy: clip views and overlaps at calendar cutoffs; train/validation use union of the first two schedule files
parameters.threshold_applies_to: unique seconds per user and canonical airing, separately in each period
parameters.threshold_rationale: Train median clipped session is 385 s. The original log has a minimum session duration of 61 s; the 60 s cut removes brief incidental programme overlaps, rather than claiming to remove source sessions below one minute. No labelled training airing is shorter than 60 s. Unlike a fraction-only cut, the rule does not penalise long programmes proportionally. Chosen using train only; no MAP or validation-based tuning.
parameters.time_coordinate: observed calendar coordinates with the missing 2020-03-29 03:00–04:00 hour removed; both sources use the same transform; no absolute timezone assigned
parameters.view_duplicates_policy: union overlapping/touching sessions per user/channel; do not count seconds twice

runtime.peak_rss_method: resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss; macOS bytes, Linux KiB converted to bytes

threshold_analysis_train_only.scope: train only; validation statistics are not used to select the threshold
threshold_analysis_train_only.unit: sum of unique observed seconds for one user and one canonical airing within train
